newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent marked down after overnight losses.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent marked down after overnight losses.

text.p: September Brent futures were cautiously marked lower on SIMEX on Thursday in line with lower performances from overnight markets.
The prospect of rapid Iraqi crude sales in August undermined both Brent and NYMEX overnight, outweighing sentiment over a tightening gasoline market in the United States.
At the Asian midday on Thursday, front-month September Brent was untraded but quoted at $18.30/$18.40 per barrel after London fell seven cents.
NYMEX August crude was last traded at $19.67 per barrel on ACCESS, regaining the two cents lost in New York trading.
The United Nations confirmed on Wednesday that Iraq would be required to sell $1 billion of oil by the end of the first week of September.
That raised the prospect of Iraq selling over seven weeks or so the oil it otherwise would have been able to sell over three months.
The oil accord with the U.N. allows sales of $2 billion over six months in two sets of 90-day periods.

When Iraqi crude sales resume is still open to question so the exact period over which the sales will have to take place is not known. But the pace of sales will have to be faster that during the first half of 1997.
